Treatment Summary
The patient is a synthetic claimant presenting with lumbar strain following a collision sustained while the vehicle was
turning left, when the patient's vehicle was struck by another vehicle. The mechanism and force of impact are
consistent with the reported low back injury. Over the course of care, the patient attended 30 visits consisting of
physical therapy, manual therapy, home exercise instruction, and medication management. Early visits focused on
pain control and restoring range of motion, and frequency was reduced as function improved, consistent with a typical
recovery pattern. Examination revealed paraspinal muscle tenderness and reduced lumbar flexion that support the
diagnosis, while neurological screening and straight-leg raise testing were within normal limits. No prior injury to the
lumbar region is documented in the available history. Billing records reflect single charges for each service rendered
with no duplicated entries. At discharge the patient was improving and was advised to continue the home program as
needed.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.

- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
